nl.title: Eigen (custom) SSL-certificaat uploaden in CyberPanel
nl.excerpt: Eigen (custom) SSL-certificaat uploaden in CyberPanel: praktische handleiding in CyberPanel, met stappen, controles en wanneer je TripleZero iT support inschakelt.
nl.bodyHtml:
Voor OV/EV of corporate certs upload je certificate + private key (+ chain) in CyberPanel in plaats van Let’s Encrypt.

Stappen

  1. Genereer CSR indien de CA dat eist (of gebruik geleverde key).
  2. Ontvang certificaat en intermediate/chain.
  3. Upload in SSL → custom / hostname selecteren.
  4. Herlaad OpenLiteSpeed indien nodig; test SSL Labs of browser.

Let op: Plak nooit private keys in tickets of chat — gebruik beveiligd uploadkanaal.

Heb je na het volgen van deze stappen nog vragen? Neem contact op met TripleZero iT support via het ticketssysteem. Vermeld hostname, CyberPanel-URL en wat je precies ziet (foutmelding of screenshot).

Gerelateerd: SSL voor mail; HTTPS forceren.

en.title: Eigen (custom) SSL certificate uploaden in CyberPanel
en.excerpt: Request Let’s Encrypt in DirectAdmin/SSL Certificates; force HTTPS only after a valid certificate.
en.bodyHtml:
For “Eigen (custom) SSL certificate uploaden in CyberPanel”, DNS (A/AAAA) must already point at this server. Then request the certificate in DirectAdmin.

Preparation

  • A/AAAA to TripleZero iT hosting
  • DirectAdmin login
  • Apex and www if both are used

Steps

  1. Confirm the domain A/AAAA record points at this server.
  2. Sign in to DirectAdmin → SSL Certificates (or Let’s Encrypt / Free & automatic certificate).
  3. Select the domain and include www if needed.
  4. Request the certificate and wait until status is valid/issued.
  5. Force HTTPS via the panel option or .htaccess only after successful issuance.
  6. Test https://yourdomain in a private window.

Verify

  • Padlock without name mismatch
  • http redirects to https

Tip: Cover apex and www in one certificate.

Note: Forcing HTTPS without a certificate causes browser errors.

Still stuck? Open a ticket with TripleZero iT via the client panel. Include your domain name, what you already tried, and any exact error messages (text or screenshot).

Related: DNS A record, WordPress URL to HTTPS.
